stories.headline: Apple Signs Tiny Corp Driver Enabling NVIDIA and AMD eGPUs for AI on Apple Silicon Macs

key_facts.fact: Apple officially signed Tiny Corp's TinyGPU driver enabling AMD RDNA3+ and NVIDIA Ampere+ eGPUs to work on Apple Silicon Macs via Thunderbolt 3+ or USB4 ports
The driver is specifically designed for LLM and AI workloads, not gaming or general-purpose graphics acceleration
Apple's signing means developers no longer need to disable System Integrity Protection (SIP) to use external GPUs, a major security improvement over previous workarounds
Tiny Corp, led by George Hotz, developed the driver; it requires macOS 12.1+ and supports AMD RDNA3+ or NVIDIA Ampere+ GPUs

stories.headline: UK Government Courts Anthropic With London Expansion and Dual Listing Proposals

key_facts.fact: The UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology circulated proposals for Anthropic including a London office expansion and a potential dual listing on the London Stock Exchange
Plans are set to be presented to CEO Dario Amodei during his visit to the UK in late May 2026
One UK government official described a dual listing as 'the dream' but called it a 'highly unlikely outcome'
The move follows the US Defense Department classifying Anthropic as a supply-chain risk, with President Trump criticizing the company on Truth Social as a 'radical left, woke company'
Anthropic has more than 150 employees in the UK, including researchers, and counts former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak as a senior adviser; the company is valued at $380 billion

stories.headline: Study Finds Most AI Users Exhibit 'Cognitive Surrender,' Accepting Faulty LLM Outputs

key_facts.fact: Research across 1,372 participants and more than 9,000 trials found that most subjects had minimal AI skepticism and accepted faulty AI-generated reasoning without scrutiny
In controlled scenarios where researchers deliberately introduced factual errors into AI outputs, 68% of participants failed to identify the mistakes before incorporating them into their work
Workers who routinely delegated analytical tasks to language models showed measurable declines in domain-specific reasoning capabilities over the study period
Nearly two-thirds of AI chatbot users exhibit high cognitive offloading, accepting outputs without verification even when they suspect errors
Researchers noted cognitive surrender is not inherently irrational, as a statistically superior system could plausibly give better-than-human results in probabilistic settings and risk assessment

stories.headline: Microsoft Copilot Terms of Use Classify It as 'Entertainment Purposes Only,' Contradicting Marketing

key_facts.fact: Microsoft's Copilot Terms of Use, updated in October 2025, state under bold capital letters 'IMPORTANT DISCLOSURES & WARNINGS' that 'Copilot is for entertainment purposes only'
The terms warn users not to rely on Copilot for important advice, to use it at their own risk, and that Microsoft makes no warranty about the tool's responses

The disclaimer contradicts Microsoft's aggressive enterprise marketing positioning Copilot as a productivity tool, with AI researcher Gary Marcus commenting 'Imagine if calculators had to carry this warning'
Microsoft also disclaims that Copilot's responses may infringe copyrights, trademarks, or rights of privacy, and users are solely responsible for any shared outputs

stories.headline: Software Engineering Job Openings Hit 67K, Up 30% YTD, Highest in Three Years

key_facts.fact: TrueUp data shows over 67,000 software engineering job openings at tech companies globally, with 26,000 in the US alone, the highest level in three years
Software engineering listings have climbed approximately 30% since the start of 2026 and are up roughly 2x since mid-2023
TrueUp founder Amit Taylor said much of the narrative around AI replacing engineers is not grounded in job posting data, with AI-related roles specifically 'exploding'
The strong US jobs report on April 4 coincided with the data, countering fears that AI is displacing software engineers

stories.headline: xAI Adds Prompt Crafting Assistance and Voice Input to Grok Imagine

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk announced on April 4 that Grok can now help users craft effective prompts for image and video generation, lowering the barrier for users unfamiliar with prompt engineering
Grok Imagine now supports voice input, allowing users to speak ideas directly and have them converted into visual prompts
Musk highlighted voice input as particularly useful for young children who can speak but cannot type complex prompts

stories.headline: Y Combinator Parts Ways With AI Compliance Startup Delve Over Fabricated Cert Allegations

key_facts.fact: Y Combinator removed AI compliance startup Delve from its portfolio directory on April 4, a rare move from the accelerator which has backed over 4,000 companies
Anonymous whistleblower posts by 'DeepDelver' alleged Delve fabricated SOC 2 compliance certifications for hundreds of clients using auto-generated reports
Delve co-founder Selin Kocalar confirmed the split on X, saying 'YC and Delve have parted ways,' while co-founder Karun Kaushik characterized the allegations as a smear campaign
Allegations also included that Delve took an open-source tool and passed it off as proprietary work without proper license attribution

stories.headline: Planet Labs Indefinitely Withholds Iran Conflict Satellite Imagery at US Government Request

key_facts.fact: Planet Labs announced it will indefinitely withhold satellite imagery of Iran and the conflict region after the US government asked all satellite imagery providers to restrict access.
The restriction applies retroactively from March 9 and is expected to remain in place until the conflict ends. It expands upon a 14-day delay on imagery Planet Labs imposed last month.
Planet Labs will switch to a managed distribution system, releasing imagery on a case-by-case basis for urgent, mission-critical requirements or in the public interest.
The announcement was made via email to Planet Labs customers, noting the US government had asked all satellite imagery providers to cooperate.

stories.headline: Artemis II Crew Completes First Manual Piloting of Orion Spacecraft in Deep Space

key_facts.fact: NASA astronaut Christina Koch and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen manually piloted the Orion spacecraft for 41 minutes starting at 9:09 p.m. EDT on Flight Day 4, testing six-degrees-of-freedom and three-degrees-of-freedom thruster modes.
At wakeup on Flight Day 4, Orion was approximately 169,000 miles from Earth with the Moon at 110,700 miles, as the crew prepared for the lunar flyby scheduled for April 6.

The crew reviewed lunar surface features selected by NASA's science team for observation during their six-hour flyby, which begins at 2:45 p.m. on April 6 when cabin windows will point toward the Moon.

The crew captured the first-ever human-eye views of the Orientale basin, a 930 km multi-ringed impact crater on the Moon's far side that scientists use as an archetype for understanding impact basins across the solar system.
Commander Reid Wiseman and Pilot Victor Glover will repeat the manual piloting demonstration on Flight Day 8 (April 9) to gather additional spacecraft performance data.

stories.headline: Nearly Half of Planned US Data Center Builds Delayed or Canceled Over Power and Supply Shortages

key_facts.fact: Close to half of planned US data center builds this year are projected to be delayed or canceled, despite unprecedented levels of AI infrastructure investment.
Imports of high-power transformers from China surged from fewer than 1,500 units in 2022 to more than 8,000 units in 2025, highlighting dependence on Chinese electrical equipment manufacturing.
Among data centers slated for 2027, only 6.3 GW of computing infrastructure is under construction versus 21.5 GW announced, with the vast majority planned for 2028-2032 not yet having broken ground.
The six largest US hyperscalers are projected to spend approximately $700 billion this year on data center capex, nearly six times 2022 levels, according to Moody's Ratings.

stories.headline: SpaceX Starship V3 First Flight Slips From April to May as Vehicle Integration Continues

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk confirmed on X that the next Starship launch (Flight 12, the first V3 flight) is 4-6 weeks away, placing the window in early to mid-May 2026, after previously targeting late April.
Flight 12 will be the first flight of V3 hardware, a ground-up redesign stacking Booster 19 with Ship 39, featuring increased propellant capacity and more powerful Raptor 3 engines.
The V3 Starship can deliver more than 100 tons to low Earth orbit, roughly three times what V2 managed, with some estimates putting the theoretical ceiling near 200 tons with full reusability.
SpaceX fired up the V3 Starship for the first time in March ahead of the planned launch, as the company packed dozens of upgrades into the vehicle for reliability and NASA Artemis suitability.

stories.headline: Bipartisan MATCH Act Targets Ban on DUV Lithography Equipment Sales and Servicing to China

key_facts.fact: The Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act was introduced in the US House on April 2, with a Senate version being prepared by Senators Pete Ricketts (R-NE) and Andy Kim (D-NJ).

The bill would ban both the sale and servicing of DUV immersion lithography equipment to China's leading chipmakers SMIC, Hua Hong, Huawei, CXMT, and YMTC, extending beyond existing EUV-only restrictions.
ASML is directly affected as the monopoly provider of advanced lithography equipment; China accounted for 33% of ASML's revenue in 2025.

If allies don't adopt equivalent restrictions, the bill directs Commerce to invoke the foreign direct product rule to force compliance, asserting US jurisdiction over items made with American technology abroad.

stories.headline: Intel Pays $14.2B to Buy Back Apollo's 49% Stake in Ireland Fab, Regaining Full Control

key_facts.fact: Intel agreed to pay $14.2 billion (cash plus ~$6.5B in new debt) to repurchase the 49% equity stake in Fab 34 in Leixlip, Ireland, that it sold to Apollo Global Management in 2024 for $11.2 billion.
Fab 34 produces chips based on Intel 4 and Intel 3 technologies, including Core Ultra and Xeon 6 processors. Intel expects the deal to boost profit and strengthen its credit profile from 2027.
Intel shares jumped roughly 9% on the announcement, reflecting market confidence in Intel's manufacturing strategy and improved CPU demand.
The buyback price represents a roughly 27% premium over Apollo's original $11.2 billion acquisition cost in 2024.

stories.headline: US Rescues Downed F-15E Weapons Officer After 7-Hour Mission Deep Inside Iran

key_facts.fact: An F-15E Strike Eagle was shot down over southern Iran on Friday April 3; the pilot was rescued within hours but the weapons systems officer (WSO), a colonel-rank airman, remained missing for 48 hours.

The WSO was rescued on Sunday April 5 by US Special Operations with Air Force Special Warfare attachments in a mission Trump called 'one of the most daring Search and Rescue Operations in U.S History', lasting seven hours over Iran with heavy firefighting.

The CIA launched a deception campaign inside Iran, spreading disinformation that US forces had already recovered the airman, to disrupt Iran's search efforts while using 'unique capabilities' to locate him.
Iran's IRGC claimed its forces destroyed two C-130 aircraft, two Black Hawk helicopters, and an MQ-9 Reaper drone during the US rescue operation in southern Isfahan.
Iran had offered a reward of approximately $60,000 to anyone who located and turned in the missing WSO, in what appeared to be an effort to capture an American prisoner of war.

stories.headline: Trump Gives Iran 48 Hours to Reopen Strait of Hormuz or Face 'All Hell'

key_facts.fact: Trump posted on Truth Social on April 4: 'Time is running out - 48 hours before all Hell will reign down on them', demanding Iran 'make a deal or open up the Hormuz Strait'.
Trump threatened to strike Iran's power plants and bridges if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, escalating rhetoric from his previous 10-day deadline.
Iran's central military command dismissed the threat as 'a helpless, nervous, unbalanced and stupid action', with General Ali Abdollahi Aliabadi issuing the response hours later.

Indirect negotiations have been led by VP Vance and Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf, mediated by Pakistan's Field Marshal Asim Munir. Iran rejected a 15-point US plan but left the door open for further talks.

stories.headline: Strike Near Bushehr Nuclear Plant Kills Guard; IAEA Warns of 'Reddest Line' Risk

key_facts.fact: A projectile struck the premises of Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant on April 4, killing one physical protection staff member and damaging an auxiliary building — the fourth attack near the facility since the war began February 28.

IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi stated 'Nuclear power plant sites or nearby areas must never be attacked' and called for 'maximum military restraint to avoid risk of a nuclear accident', warning the strikes risk crossing the 'reddest line'.
No increase in radiation levels was reported after the attack, according to Iranian authorities confirmed by the IAEA.
Russia's Rosatom evacuated 198 more staff from Bushehr on April 4-5, with buses departing toward Armenia. Up to 50 volunteers will remain to maintain equipment and operations.
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned that strikes on Bushehr expose the entire region to the risk of radioactive contamination.
Simultaneous US-Israeli strikes hit the Mahshahr Petrochemical Special Economic Zone in Khuzestan, damaging the Bandar Imam complex and Fajr 1 and 2 plants, killing five people and injuring 170.

stories.headline: Iran Drone Strikes Hit Energy Infrastructure Across Kuwait, Bahrain, and UAE

key_facts.fact: Iranian drone attacks on April 5 damaged two Kuwaiti power and water desalination plants, shutting down two electricity-generating units and causing 'significant material damage', the Ministry of Electricity and Water reported.

Kuwait's Shuwaikh Oil Sector Complex and government Ministries Complex building were also struck, with fires reported at key facilities. Kuwait Petroleum Corporation reported 'significant material losses'.
In Bahrain, Bapco Energies confirmed an Iranian drone struck one of its oil storage facilities, causing a tank fire that was later contained with no injuries reported.
In Abu Dhabi, multiple fires broke out at the Borouge petrochemical plant from falling debris after air defense interceptions, forcing immediate suspension of operations pending damage assessment.
The UAE Ministry of Defence said it intercepted 23 ballistic missiles and 56 UAVs launched from Iran, with interceptor debris damaging a residential tower in Abu Dhabi's marina area.

stories.headline: Russia's VPN Crackdown Triggers Nationwide Banking Outage, Durov Links to Telegram Ban

key_facts.fact: Sberbank, VTB, and T-Bank all experienced service outages on April 3, affecting mobile banking, ATM withdrawals, payment transfers, and Russia's Fast Payment System. The Moscow Metro was forced to allow free entry.

Telegram founder Pavel Durov on April 4 blamed Russia's VPN crackdown for the outage, stating that 65 million Russians still use Telegram daily via VPNs despite the ban, and the government's VPN blocking broke banking infrastructure.
Roskomnadzor demanded Russian media remove reports linking the banking outage to government internet blocking measures, including articles from Forbes Russia and the Mash Telegram channel.

Moscow has intensified a crackdown on internet use and Telegram, pushing Russians to adopt a state-run 'super-app' called Max modeled after China's WeChat. Digital Development Minister Shadayev on March 30 said the government will 'reduce the use of VPNs'.

stories.headline: Artemis II Enters Moon's Gravitational Sphere as Crew Prepares for Historic Flyby

key_facts.fact: Artemis II entered the Moon's sphere of influence on April 5 — the point where lunar gravity exerts more force on the Orion spacecraft than Earth's gravity — ahead of the first crewed lunar flyby since Apollo 17 in 1972.
The lunar flyby is scheduled for Monday April 6 and will last up to five hours, during which the crew will photograph the lunar surface including areas of the far side never seen directly by humans.
The crew — NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen — launched on April 1 from Kennedy Space Center aboard SLS.
On Flight Day 3 (April 4), the crew conducted spacesuit tests on Easter Sunday and prepared the cabin configuration for the lunar flyby approach.

stories.headline: UK Proposes London Expansion and Dual Listing to Woo Anthropic After US Defense Clash

key_facts.fact: The UK's Department for Science, Innovation and Technology has circulated proposals for Anthropic including a London office expansion and potential dual listing, to be presented to CEO Dario Amodei during a late May UK visit.

The courtship follows the US Defense Department classifying Anthropic as a supply-chain risk after the company refused to allow Claude for military surveillance or autonomous weapons. A federal judge temporarily blocked the blacklisting.
Anthropic has approximately 200 UK employees and appointed former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak as a senior adviser. The company is preparing a potential October 2026 IPO at a $380 billion valuation.
London Mayor Sadiq Khan wrote to Amodei inviting Anthropic, stating: 'London can provide a stable, proportionate and pro-innovation environment.'

stories.headline: March 2026 Confirmed as Hottest March in 48-Year US Satellite Temperature Record

key_facts.fact: Satellite data confirmed March 2026 as clearly the warmest March in the 48-year satellite temperature record for the contiguous US states, substantially exceeding the previous record set in 2012.

The March heat wave set over 7,000 daily high-temperature records, nearly 2,000 monthly records, with 160+ cities recording their hottest March on record and 17 states setting new statewide March highs.

A new all-time US daily high temperature record for any March day of 112°F was set during the Southwest heat wave, which Yale Climate Connections ranked as one of the six most astonishing weather events of the century.

Despite record US warmth, the global satellite temperature anomaly for March was +0.38°C, and averaged over all Northern Hemisphere land areas March 2026 was 'uneventful, and was even cooler than 2024 and 2025'.
Across South and Southeast Asia, up to two billion people have been affected by extreme heat, with temperatures running 7 to 12 degrees above normal in early 2026.
